title: The unitary method
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The unitary method (finding the value of one unit, then scaling) is a basic proportional reasoning technique, while the bank point teaches derivatives as rates of change, which is a different idea at a much higher depth.}

draft.title: The unitary method
card: The unitary method finds the value of one unit first. A unit can be one item, one litre, one hour or 1 per cent. Then you scale up by multiplying.
To find one unit, divide the total amount by the number of units. If 5 kg of rice costs $12.50, then 1 kg costs $12.50 ÷ 5 = $2.50.
To find several units, multiply the one-unit value by the number wanted. 3 kg of that rice costs 3 × $2.50 = $7.50.
To compare two deals, find the cost of one unit for each. The smaller cost per unit is the better buy.
draft.remember: Divide to get one unit, then multiply to get the amount you need.

a.q: Four tickets to a footy match cost $90. Using the unitary method, what do seven tickets at the same price cost?
a.why: One ticket costs $90 ÷ 4 = $22.50, so seven cost 7 × $22.50 = $157.50. $22.50 is only the cost of one ticket, so it stops after the first step.
a.clue: Find the cost of one ticket first.

b.q: Ava can buy 6 pens for $4.50 or 10 pens for $7.20 at a shop in Bendigo. Which is the better buy, and why?
b.why: 6 pens: $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 each. 10 pens: $7.20 ÷ 10 = $0.72 each. The lower cost per pen is the better buy, so the pack of 10 wins even though it costs more in total.
b.clue: Work out the cost of one pen in each pack.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($90 ÷ 4 × 7 = $157.50; 72 cents per pen beats 75 cents), and the card and remember line are accurate and stay within this point.
